scope: Read-only source/material audit of retained R06 candidate-03 and its R04/R05 inheritance; new diagnostic helper only. No product, ancestor, pose, geometry, shader authoring or original-evidence edits.
target: Narrow hard-looking lower inner edge next to teeth in jaw and speak. The visibly rounded exterior lip body is not assumed to lack bulk.

firstJudgment.confirmed: R04 restored continuous oral-skin material responsibility; R05 repaired selected return-surface motion ownership; R06 candidate-03 changes peripheral pucker continuity while protecting lip core/rim/contact samples. These versions do not establish measured rim thickness or full surface contact.
firstJudgment.priority: First separate a shader/semantic seam from a geometric turn/contact-boundary defect at the actual visible lower edge.
notProven: The mesh lacks a connected inner return.
The lower lip body needs to become thicker.
The current visible hard edge is caused by wetness, l19Oral, psH or one particular contact step.
A scalar material thickness value or paired gap measures anatomical lip-edge thickness.

observations: The lower external lip remains visibly rounded with a broad highlight. Close to the teeth it terminates in a much narrower, comparatively straight inner band.

The inner band and the cavity border remain readable from the oblique jaw view; a screenshot alone cannot distinguish an abruptly turned continuous surface, a material transition or actual insufficient cross-sectional depth.
Existing coarse tooth shapes and cavity shading affect edge contrast. They are separate native materials and must not be recoloured to claim a lip-edge repair.
directImageReview.causalBoundary: No current R06 material ablation or section measurement has yet been rendered for this R07 audit.

materialGeometryCoupling.mechanism: H5 maps native oral_skin_ids through canonical recipes to l19Oral; the indexed display subdivision interpolates attributes. Kl clamps this into samples.inner for skin and l19State.x. R04 liOral is clamp(l19State.x)*skinCoverage*(1-step(.5,csType)); it is not a measured wet-dry junction or thickness field.
materialGeometryCoupling.constraint: Keep actual csType/material-slot attribution. Native teeth/gums/tongue remain on viewer.skin.material; the helper changes only headProceduralSkin.material(). A color line following liOral does not itself prove a geometric boundary.

materialGeometryCoupling.mechanism: R04 blends a native mucosa color/roughness/coat endpoint once by liWeight, fades shader height psH by 1-liWeight, and applies .12+.88*exp(-max(0,l19Detail.w)*120) to outgoing light. R02 exterior coverage instead uses rest rails, front/lateral fade, and a normalized rail-depth wet band.
materialGeometryCoupling.constraint: l19Detail.w on oral surfaces is current mouth-forward depth normalized by mouth scale, not optical path or rim thickness. psH masking can contribute derivative terms at a semantic transition; its existence in code is not a visible-cause finding.

materialGeometryCoupling.mechanism: R02/R04 still choose upper/lower optical endpoints with a hard rest-rail midline classifier. R05 computes a different smooth motion carrier for selected negative-v return vertices from fixed jaw-reference distances, without changing those material labels. A return region may therefore move with one lip while retaining the other optical endpoint.
materialGeometryCoupling.support: R05 recorded 6641 changed ownership vertices in the retained baseline; that global count does not identify the current visible lower-edge pixels.
materialGeometryCoupling.minimalCheck: At actual contributing lower-edge triangles, compare rest-based upper, native v/inner/red/depth, material slot and the R05 carrier when available. If no mismatched region contributes to the defect, reject this explanation.
materialGeometryCoupling.constraint: Do not simply blend upper/lower palettes globally. Motion carrier is an engineering construction, not automatically an anatomical material label.

source: R06 preview: Ql closure and dental envelope
materialGeometryCoupling.mechanism: Kl selects 49 opposing rim samples. Ql computes a mouth-up projected pair gap and applies interpolated vertical closure. Its dental/gum/tongue frontal-envelope correction then only processes i.lips with .05 <= native v <= 1.05; v<.05 is skipped. Eligible points are pushed along mouth front toward envelopeDepth+.00016*scale, capped at .004*scale.
materialGeometryCoupling.hypothesis: A hard response boundary near v=.05 could create or preserve a sharp cross-sectional turn adjacent to a near-tooth inner band.
materialGeometryCoupling.minimalCheck: Locate the visible edge on original indexed triangles; record both endpoints of edges straddling v=.05, their surface tangent/normal, current front coordinates and any actual envelope correction. The hypothesis fails if the displayed hard turn does not align with that response boundary or no differential correction occurs.
materialGeometryCoupling.constraint: The .00009*scale minimum paired gap is an authored closure tolerance, not anatomical lip-edge thickness. Pair-gap success and front-envelope protection do not prove finite-area contact, whole-mesh nonintersection or continuous collision detection.

materialGeometryCoupling.mechanism: R02 scales original coarse furrow microGeometry during native evaluation. Ql runs local motion, closure and envelope correction, recomputes mesh normals, adds atlas displacement along those normals using red/strain/pressure/inner factors, then recomputes normals again. The later procedural shader psH is a separate normal perturbation.
materialGeometryCoupling.constraint: The no-bump experiment resets normal to fbGeomN after psH; it retains all evaluated geometry, mesh normals and native coarse relief. If the edge remains, it only refutes this shader-relief contribution as necessary, not all normal/geometry causes.

materialGeometryCoupling.mechanism: R06 protects native lips, rim, contact samples and one-ring core plus the center, and excludes oral/negative-v edits. It is an exact no-op for the tested jaw and speak states, so those edge shapes remain inherited R05 results.
materialGeometryCoupling.constraint: Retain this accepted peripheral pucker correction and original 49 contact samples unless a separately justified R07 contact design explicitly changes the contract. A local edge fix must not be achieved by weakening full-mouth motion or reopening a closed mouth.

thicknessDefinitions.visibleBandWidth: Projected width of a rendered strip; depends on camera, occlusion and albedo, and is not a physical thickness measurement.
thicknessDefinitions.vermilionHeight: External inner-to-outer rail distance; does not specify the lower return curvature or wet-dry contact region.
thicknessDefinitions.localReturnProfile: Connected original-index cross-section from external vermilion through the turn into the oral return, in a documented local frame. Its extent and tangent rotation can diagnose a sharp fold without pretending it is a full enclosed volume.
thicknessDefinitions.enclosedTissueThickness: Requires supported opposing tissue surfaces/section correspondence and an anatomical definition. Neither l19Oral nor l19Detail.w provides that measurement.

materialThicknessProperty.meaning: Both actual material thickness values are 0 with transmission 0. This is a rendering parameter state, not proof that the mesh has zero geometric tissue thickness.

externalFirstPartyFact.title: The dirty lip trick
externalFirstPartyFact.sourceType: First-party clinical surgical-technique note, original publisher PDF, authors at British Columbia Children's Hospital, Canada; metadata independently checked on US NLM PubMed.
externalFirstPartyFact.access: Original one-page PDF full text read through web retrieval; PMC full-page route showed a browser-check page and was not relied upon as read full text.
externalFirstPartyFact.supportedFact: The wet-dry/red line marks the transition between oral mucosa and lip vermilion and serves as a surgical anatomical landmark.
externalFirstPartyFact.inferenceForThisAudit: A material tissue-transition label and a geometric cut/turn are different concepts. The current l19Oral mask cannot be declared the physiological wet-dry line without checking its actual surface location.
doesNotSupply: A numerical healthy lip-edge thickness target for this person.
A roll radius or deformation rule.
A reason to map general whole-lip thickness statistics onto the displayed narrow edge.

inheritedDiagnosticEvidence.basis: R05 diagnosis-02 on immutable R04; original QA and independent visual review are hash-listed above.
inheritedDiagnosticEvidence.supported: The older central thin slit and tooth fragments remained when procedural shader relief was bypassed and in albedo; removing closure position updates widened the opening. This justified separating surface shading from closure/geometry.
inheritedDiagnosticEvidence.boundary: That experiment predates R05 carrier correction and R06. It is a prior that guides current testing, not current R06 proof, and does not justify disabling closure.

perPoseSequence: Render current R06 original and capture full state, actual shader and geometric samples.
Open frozen-surface diagnostic window; render no-bump with all evaluated native buffers, original settings, camera and lights held exact.
Render final-albedo output with the same frozen surface.
Restore original compile/cache descriptors; render original again and require full state, pixels, actual shader and R05/R06 calls exact.
interpretation: Loss of a line only in no-bump implicates shader relief but does not repair geometry. Persistence rules out that particular detail perturbation as necessary.

Albedo retains authored tissue colours and the actual surface silhouette/occlusion while removing lighting and the oral-depth multiplier. A line disappearing in albedo may be a shading cue; that alone does not prove a semantic or geometric cause.

Combine actual visible-triangle labels with original-index cross-sections. A physically continuous return with a palette-only seam calls for material responsibility review; an abrupt tangent turn retained by no-bump points toward evaluated geometry; missing/degenerate return connectivity would be a different structural problem.
constraints: No geometry, semantic, canonical, original native uniform or source-parameter mutation.
No material cloning, new sheet, global thickening, arbitrary darker strip or lower wetness as the result.
Avoid R06 report/update/pose calls during a temporary compile-hook window; compatibility protection must remain intact.
After restore, compare actual attached GPU shader source rather than trusting only the cached innerLip.shaderEvidence template.
Do not use screenshot band width, material thickness or pair gap as anatomical thickness.

diagnosticHelper.status: Diagnostic only; no production repair and no actual R07 GPU evidence yet.
diagnosticHelper.asyncHashRule: WebCrypto SHA-256 tasks are tracked by pendingHashes; wait for zero, require hashEvidenceComplete and errors=[] before persisting records.
diagnosticHelper.nativeSafety: Original-mode install is observational. A single new uniform selects two tightly anchored fragment operations. No native setter, render or update is called. All existing compile-stage uniform objects are retained; original 15 shared native uniform identities and values are checked.
diagnosticHelper.cacheReviewFix: Root source review caught that a repeated static cache key could reuse a prior window's program/control without onBeforeCompile. Each install now uses a unique monotonic /window-N diagnostic suffix, capped at 16 windows; restore returns the exact original function/descriptor/cache value.
diagnosticHelper.testBoundary: The synthetic fixture checks this helper's state/ownership/cache logic only. It neither creates a native GPU frame nor establishes visual or actual Three compilation success; those remain the root runner's gates.

nextDecision: Await matched current R06 no-bump/albedo frames and read-only section/semantic evidence before choosing a production R07 mechanism. Prioritize the lower edge near teeth, preserve existing outer lip bulk and accepted R06 pucker continuity.
